guide.text: Prototype guide: press Play on a board with the blue mark. Try First-Run Setup, then Continue and Finish to land on Shop. In Shop, tap the cheese name for Deal Detail, Add to trip for the Trip, and the Deals/Trip/Radar selector. In Pantry try Scan, Voice and the Olive oil row. In Plan try the preferences chip, View dish and Sign in to use. The avatar opens Account and Settings. On iPad the sidebar and icon rail switch tabs. Loading, empty and AI error boards are static.

shop.text: Shop: the home tab. Top of screen is deals, not setup. ZIP and stores are a read-only line that links to Settings. The long ad-cycle notice becomes one freshness line. Trip (shopping list) and Radar are sections of Shop. 'Have it' is a quiet secondary action, never required.

pantry.text: Pantry: its own destination. Add by search, scan (v1.6.2) or voice (version TBD). Nothing is required: the banner says so. Yes/No per ingredient, as in v1.6.0. Sync status stays visible but quiet.

pantry-idea.text: Idea, post-MVP: keep the first choice a plain Yes/No. After choosing Yes, optionally drill down to 'Have Lots' or 'Have a Little' via long press, +/- buttons or multi-press. Amount never blocks the Yes.

plan.text: Plan: works with no pantry data. Pantry-aware savings show as an optional hint that can be dismissed. Preferences are a summary chip that opens an editor. AI chef shows a sign-in state for guests (v1.7).

settings.text: Account and Settings: opened from the header avatar on every tab. Location and stores live here only (no per-trip override). Also holds preferences, sync, AI sign-in, notifications and links to Data Explorer, API docs and legal.

onboarding.text: First Run: ZIP and stores, once. Skippable, with the current default applied. Guests keep it on the device and it syncs after sign-in. A second skippable step covers dietary and macro preferences.

ipad-shop.text: iPad Shop (landscape): sidebar for Shop, Pantry and Plan, with the account at the bottom. Deals list on the left, the selected deal's detail on the right. Same content and the same quiet 'Have It' as iPhone; the detail pane is where price history and club benchmarks get room.

ipad-pantry.text: iPad Pantry (landscape): ingredient list on the left, optional details on the right. The detail pane shows where the ingredient is used in this week's plan, never as a requirement. Scan and Voice entries sit beside search.

ipad-plan.text: iPad Plan (landscape): dishes on the left, the selected dish on the right with ingredients tagged 'At Home' or priced from Shop. 'Add Missing to Trip' is the single primary action.

ipad-settings.text: iPad Account and Settings: a centered form sheet over the current screen instead of a full-screen page. Same sections and order as iPhone.

ipad-portrait.text: iPad Shop (portrait): the sidebar collapses to an icon rail so the deals list keeps the width, shown as a two-column grid. Tapping a deal opens its detail as a sheet. The iPad mini uses this layout.

r2-trip.text: Shop: Trip. Leads with the best plan (two-store split) and the one-stop alternative. Items are grouped by store with check-off. Coupons, export and print are secondary actions. Replaces the old Shopping List and Cart Bridge tab.

r2-radar.text: Shop: Radar. Three short sections: Stock-Up Alerts (6-week lows), Hold Off (cycle peaks, with a substitute), and Club vs. Store. USDA movers and pipeline status move behind 'Details' so they stop crowding the top.

r2-scan.text: Pantry: Scan Barcode (v1.6.2). The camera is optional: typing the barcode is always available. A scan proposes a generic ingredient; nothing is added until the user confirms or corrects the match.

r2-voice.text: Pantry: Add by Voice (version TBD). Dictate, review what was heard, then confirm. Each item shows its match and can be edited or removed. Unmatched items can be added as custom ingredients. Nothing is added until 'Add Items'.

r2-prefs.text: Plan: Preferences. Servings, macro goal, dietary restrictions and cookware in one editor, reached from the summary chip on Plan and from Settings. Every choice has an 'Any' or 'None' default.

r2-ai-error.text: Plan: AI Chef (service error). Signed in, but the service is unavailable. The error is a banner with 'Try Again'; the standard deterministic suggestions stay on screen, so the screen is never empty (v1.7).

r2-ai-out.text: Plan: AI Chef (signed out). A guest sees why sign-in is needed and a clear 'Sign In' action, plus 'Keep Using Standard Suggestions'. No API key field (removed in v1.7). Manual planning is never blocked.

r2-onb2.text: First-Run Setup, step 2: optional dietary and macro preferences. Skippable, and editable later in Settings. Defaults to Any.

r2-ipad-pantry.text: iPad Pantry (portrait): icon rail plus a full-width list. An ingredient's details open as a sheet. iPad mini uses this layout.

r2-ipad-plan.text: iPad Plan (portrait): icon rail plus wide dish cards. A dish opens as a sheet with ingredients and 'Add Missing to Trip'. iPad mini uses this layout.

r3-title.text: V2.0 Wireframes, Round 3: Detail and State Screens

r3-shop-detail.text: Shop: Deal Detail. Pushed from a deal card. Price, 6-week history and the club/store comparison get full width. 'Add to Trip' is the single primary action; 'Have It' stays quiet and optional.

r3-pantry-detail.text: Pantry: Ingredient Detail. Yes/No at the top, optional details below (never required), where it is used in this week's plan, and whether it is on sale. Removing is a quiet text action.

r3-dish.text: Plan: Dish Detail. Cost per serving and macros first, then ingredients tagged 'At Home' or priced by store. 'Add Missing to Trip' is the primary action, so the pantry is used but never required.

r3-loading.text: Shop: Loading. Skeleton cards keep the layout stable while prices load. The header, selector and tab bar are usable immediately; the freshness line says prices are updating.

r3-trip-empty.text: Shop: Empty Trip. Explains how items get here (from Deals or from a dish in Plan) and offers one next step in each direction. No error styling: an empty Trip is normal.

r3-pantry-empty.text: Pantry: First Visit. Reassures that Pantry is optional, then offers the three ways to add: scan, voice, or a few common staples. Nothing is preselected.
